sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1995. Digging for the roots of language death in Eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. Paper presented at the 69th Annual Meeting of the Linguistic Society of America, New Orleans, 5-8 Jan 1995. 19 pp. ERIC document ED384231.
sources.note: Nothing about Moksela (no Moksela data exist). Sec. 2 table (p.4) lists 'Moksela (Maksela, Opselan) — extinct (1974)' as a dialect under the language KAYELI, placement based partly on 'indirect evidence such as written historical records, and local oral history, and place names'. The only stress remark in the paper is about Kayeli proper (p.8, sec. 3.2): 'The Kayeli enclitics are extrametrical, not affecting penultimate stress on the root.'

sources.note: This work describes Kayeli (kaye1241), with comparative material on Buru and Hukumina; Moksela (moks1249) appears only once, as an extinct dialect listed under KAYELI in the language-geography table (p. 4, printed p. 2), with no linguistic data. No catalog entry for moks1249 and nothing usable here: the paper lists Moksela as an extinct dialect of the Kayeli language and gives no forms, no stress and no tone statement.
